title: How do Macdonald star factors interact with the CTMC normalization?
question: Take a partition \lambda with \lambda_n=0 and let S_n(\lambda) be the content-fixed sector used for the modified Macdonald CTMC. The claimed stationary law is \pi(\mu)=F_{\mu}^*(x;1,t)/P_{\lambda}^*(x;1,t), yet the jump rates are written in terms of the unstarred polynomials and truncated geometric normalizations [m]_t=\frac{1-t^m}{1-t}. Why is it legitimate to replace every F_{\mu}^* with F_{\mu} divided by the product b_{\mu}(1,t)=\prod_{s\in\mu}(1-t^{1+\mathrm{leg}(s)}) and to normalize globally by P_{\lambda}^*(x;1,t)=\sum_{\nu\in S_n(\lambda)}F_{\nu}^*(x;1,t)? In other words, how do we prove that the star/non-star conversion is purely multiplicative and therefore compatible with the local clock probabilities in the CTMC construction?

nodes.text: if a transition changes m_i(\mu) then the factor b_{\mu}(1,t) updates by the same truncated geometric weight
